question: List the standard error of the mean and t statistic formulas given in the statistics formula reference notes.
answer: The provided statistics formula reference notes do not contain the standard error of the mean or t statistic formulas.

S1.title: Statistics Reference Notes
S1.text:
INFERENCE
95% confidence interval for a mean (sigma known): x-bar +/- 1.96 * sigma / sqrt(n)
t statistic: t = (x-bar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n)), with n - 1 degrees of freedom
Type I error rate = alpha. Power = 1 - beta.
Chi-square statistic: sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)

S2.title: Statistics Reference Notes
S2.text:
DESCRIPTIVE FORMULAS
Mean: x-bar = (sum of x) / n
Population variance: sigma^2 = sum((x - mu)^2) / N
Sample variance: s^2 = sum((x - x-bar)^2) / (n - 1)
Standard deviation: the square root of the variance.
IQR = Q3 - Q1. Outlier fences: Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR.
Coefficient of variation: CV = standard deviation / mean.

S4.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S4.text:
Statistics Theory Notes
Statistics & Probability - independently written demonstration notes. Not official university material.

S5.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
S5.text:
3. The Bootstrap
The bootstrap estimates the uncertainty of a statistic by resampling. Draw n observations with
replacement from the original sample of size n, compute the statistic, and repeat this B times, for
example B = 1000. The spread of the B statistics approximates the sampling variability.
A bootstrap percentile interval for 95% confidence uses the 2.5th and the 97.5th percentiles of the
B bootstrap statistics. The bootstrap needs no formula for the standard error, which makes it useful
for medians and other awkward statistics.
